Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, Japan); secondary: Eurozone, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Middle East (Gulf/Iran)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The yen is hovering near 160/USD amid rising BOJ rate hike expectations (73% priced for September), supported by U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent's unusual public pressure on Japan to act. Simultaneously, the USD faces conflicting forces: Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut has pushed September Fed hike odds to 65% (up from 41%), yet the dollar remains soft — markets appear skeptical whether hawkishness alone restores Fed credibility. A Gulf conflict escalation sent Brent above $91 and pushed 10Y Treasury yields to their highest since January 2025, with JGB 10Y hitting 3% for the first time in 30 years. Key U.S. economic data later this week will be critical for pricing further Fed tightening.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — heavily so. US yields at multi-month highs, Fed hike odds surging, Warsh's hawkish tone, and USD dynamics are central threads throughout.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85
Probability of increase: 65% (as per CME FedWatch cited in the article for September)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15
Probability of holding: 35%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0
Probability of decrease: ~0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 65 (Meaningfully more hawkish than before — Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks drove a sharp repricing from 41% to 65% hike probability in one week; however, dollar weakness signals residual market skepticism about Fed follow-through, capping the hawkish read slightly)
